title: Representing Addition and Subtraction
keyIdea: Addition and subtraction can be represented with objects, drawings, and mental images such as fingers — not only with written number sentences. Showing 3 + 2 with cubes, a sketch, or raised fingers is the same sum.
familyTip: Ask your child to show 4 + 1 three ways: with counters, a quick drawing, and fingers. Then try 5 − 2 the same three ways.

visual.caption: Fair representation or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it then a box.

items: fingers never count as a model

lab.caption: Flagship lab: objects for +/−, draw the story, fingers, catch digits-only myth.

kid: You can show adding with objects. Put 3 here and 2 there, then join them.
You can also draw the story, or put up fingers. That still shows the same sum.
For take-away, start with objects and remove some. Count what is left.
Writing 3 + 2 = 5 is fine later — first show it with things, pictures, or fingers.
adult: CCSS K.OA.1 / NC Y1: represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
Words: represent, objects, drawing, fingers, altogether, take away. Common mistakes: only writing numerals; thinking fingers are cheating; skipping a concrete model for subtraction.
In the lab your child joins 3+2 objects, draws 4+1, shows fingers, takes 2 from 5, and spots the digits-only mix-up.
